items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

items.summary: ADR1D is a reproducible synthetic benchmark for one-dimensional advection-dispersion-reaction transport. It contains 300 parameterized scenarios, 749,700 analytical space-time concentration records, and 88,200 noisy virtual-sensor observations. Fixed scenario-level training, validation, and test partitions support leakage-aware forward, inverse, reconstruction, and arrival-detection studies. The release includes the complete generation configuration, a machine-readable data dictionary, dependency-free Python generation and validation scripts, and validation records.
items.title: ADR1D: A Reproducible One-Dimensional Advection-Dispersion-Reaction Benchmark Dataset

items.summary: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the second-order total generalized variation functional. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice. Comparisons with related spatial image reconstruction algorithms show comparable reconstruction results. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging, where the proposed functional improves the state of the art.
items.title: Total Generalized Variation for Inverse Problems Involving Piecewise Linear Finite Elements

items.summary: Differentiable Photon Transport — Volume I: Foundations , by Chris von Csefalvay, is an instructional book on differentiable photon transport using X-ray and C-arm imaging. It develops the geometry, transmission, spectral and detector models, stochastic transport, differentiation, registration, reconstruction and acquisition design alongside executable NVIDIA Warp/CUDA examples. Version 1.0.0 includes the public book source and a built static website. The website archive preserves the interactive figures, recorded numerical display data and source listings. Expensive transport calculations run outside the browser; their recorded outputs retain their provenance and stated limitations. The live book is available at photontransport.com . items.title: Differentiable Photon Transport — Volume I: Foundations

items.summary: Bridge assessment treats inspection, structural analysis and damage identification as sequential, separated steps. Concealed damage is assumed based on indirect information resulting in speculative values. An integrated, cloud-based workflow that automates the pipeline from drone-acquired point clouds to damage-aware BIM/FEM analysis and nondestructive concealed damage identification is introduced, which accelerates the overall process and provides a real as-is degraded bridge model, which provides reliable bridge assessment. The total process is designed as a highly automated BIMification process and implemented in the cloud with one access point, which speeds up the whole process. The process is presented in two parts. Part 1 covers the reconstruction of the geometrical BIM model from the measured point cloud obtained by UAV-based RGB and LiDAR observations, whereas in this paper, Part 2 introduces concealed damage identification by applying an inverse simulation-based damage analysis. The simulation-based system identification compares computed deformations of candidate damage models with observed deformations, while beforehand a robust sensitivity analysis identifies system-relevant damages, which are then considered. A distributed asynchronous task queue orchestrates large-scale, parallel computation of remote generation of damage variants, automated execution of structural analyses, post-processing, and creation of evaluation results. The platform readily integrates with web frameworks and common brokers and supports concurrent execution. A case study with a real motorway-bridge demonstrates that the proposed new damage identification method, automation and cloudification markedly accelerate assessment and enable prompt, reliable estimation of residual structural capacity, closing a critical gap in post-event safety evaluation.
items.title: From Drone Observed Bridge Displacements to Concealed Damage Identification and Assessment

items.summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Author identity is withheld pending the outcome of review. The package contains two independently generated archives: (1) model-I-single-branch/ — a single clock-controlled ternary LFSR generator over GF(3) (controller LFSR A + data LFSR B), together with its exact period and design-condition checkers, a statistical analysis suite, a 14-family ternary long-sequence test battery, and a cryptanalytic attack suite (basic correlation, embedding, fast correlation, Berlekamp-Massey reconstruction, and a linear-consistency/clock-control attack). Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
items.title: Reproducibility package for "Clock-Controlled Ternary Sequence Generators over GF(3): Exact Periods, Statistical Structure, and Cryptanalytic Comparison of Single-Branch and Three-Branch Nonlinear Architectures"

items.summary: Clinical timelines support treatment-window analysis and leakage-free modeling, but discharge summaries often obscure chronology and structured EHR tables describe only part of the patient course. We present a UID-preserving framework that links each narrative event occurrence to its source span and retains that identity through text-only estimation, structured-evidence retrieval, timestamped source-row grounding, and joint revision. We also present GAVEL, an LLM judge that compares two UID-aligned timelines against the narrative and structured record, to augment prior matching and temporal assessments. Across six open-weight models and 40 mixed-critical-care summaries, the GLM 5.2 multimodal revision, as compared to its text-only variant, improved temporal agreement without reducing event recovery and performed competitively with clinician annotations, while other model revisions showed smaller gains and lower overall performance. Ablations showed that UIDs primarily preserve event retention, whereas source-row linkage supports temporal placement. Blinded human review upheld most GAVEL findings, and controlled adjudication favored multimodal over text-only GLM 5.2 but did not for DeepSeek V3.2. In developing the UID and judge pipeline, we are able to demonstrate 43\% increased event recovery, a framework competitive with clinician annotations, and a system with occurrence-level provenance for both reconstruction and evaluation.
items.title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication

items.summary: The contemporary discourse of "media ethics" rests on a terminological error. The corpus keyword is FREE SPEECH — the first liberty of the Gordon–Trenchard tradition (Cato's Letters, 1720–23) — not the later, softer vocabulary of media ethics, which presupposes a neutral structure that does not exist. Media is not neutral structure; it is an appetite. This essay distinguishes authentic free speech (civic speech addressed to communities about matters of common concern) from its three principal perversions — the speech of warmongers, pornographers, and advertisers — and documents the claim through a fifty-year publishing record: Media Free Times: A Random Sampling of Anarchic Communications Art (1972–present), a multimedia periodical operating across microfilm, audio cassette, and print, with production and preservation processes developed in direct experimental exchange with Library and Archives Canada in the 1970s. The essay records the free-speech-movement origins at San Jose State under Prof. Phil Jacqueline, the first Free Speech Messages (FSM) broadcasts via the Bay Area Committee for Public Access, the Virtual Free University concept and its anticipatory cross-media date index, and the documented lifecycle of archival suppression at Library and Archives Canada — including the reconstruction that was once coherent and fully linked, with the archive itself on record calling it a precursor of web pages. The transition from open-source FSM to closed-loop TED is named info dysinformation architecture: the architecture retained, the openness excised. The remedy proposed is twofold — restoration of the free-speech vocabulary and systematic recovery, in the twelve-step tradition, from the engineered appetites (sucrose, spectacle, surveillance) that make the perversion economy profitable. Keywords: free speech; media ethics; info dysinformation architecture; FSM; TED; Media Free Times; Virtual Free University; Media Anonymous; sucrose; attention commons; Cato's Letters; propaganda; Jacques Ellul; Neil Postman; data preservation; copper sheets
items.title: MEDIA ETHICS AND FREE SPEECH — OR THE LACK THEREOF From Open-Source FSM to Closed-Loop TED, and the Recovery of the First Liberty

items.summary: For the Jacobi family with parameters $(0,β)$, $β\geq-1/3$, we prove a continuous comparison theorem for the associated weighted Jacobi--Radau functions. When two consecutive functions are parametrised by the same Prüfer phase, the function of higher degree attains that phase closer to $θ=0$ and has strictly larger amplitude. In particular, the moduli of all corresponding relative extrema increase strictly with the degree. The lower bound $-1/3$ is sharp for this continuous statement: when $-1<β<-1/3$, the amplitude inequality is reversed at sufficiently small positive phases. This local reversal does not determine the optimal range for the discrete extremal inequalities. For $-1/3\leqβ\leq0$, the positive Jacobi product formula identifies the endpoint values of the Lebesgue functions with the global Lebesgue constants, so $(Λ_n^{(0,β)})_{n\geq0}$ is strictly increasing. At $β=0$ the weighted Radau functions reduce to $P_m^{(0,-1)}$. We thereby recover the theorem of Wong and Zhang and obtain, through an exact total-variation formula, a short proof of the Qu--Wong theorem on Legendre Lebesgue constants. The representation and the termwise comparison together realise the alternative-expression approach proposed by Qu and Wong, without asymptotic expansions, error bounds, or finite numerical verification. The proof is based on the equal-phase Prüfer architecture developed in the first author's earlier preprint arXiv:2608.01404; it applies that architecture to the problem posed by Qu and Wong.
items.title: Equal-Phase Monotonicity for Weighted Jacobi-Radau Functions and Jacobi Lebesgue Constants

One firewall runs throughout: a structure's form may cross domains, a bare number never. No physical grade is raised; the Clay mass gap and the empirical Koide value stay open. items.summary: We present XMST, an extended minimum spanning tree framework for identifying spatially coherent stellar structures using an objective, data-driven fracture-scale criterion. XMST combines percolation analysis with Jenks Natural Breaks optimisation, restricting the MST edge-length distribution to the subcritical regime before determining the final fracture scale. The method was validated using 1000 controlled Monte Carlo realisations containing eight empirical stellar-association templates, including a deliberately overlapping pair. The Percolation-Jenks fracture scale was highly reproducible, with a median of 17.028 pc and a between-realisation standard deviation of 0.066 pc. The injected structures were recovered with a mean completeness of 0.9996 and mean purity of 0.7413, while alternative CDF and Mean Edge criteria selected substantially larger fracture scales and produced markedly lower purities. Propagation of the published distance uncertainties through 10,000 additional XMST reconstructions produced a median absolute fracture-scale change of only 0.282 pc. Under these perturbations, mean completeness was 0.8605 and mean purity 0.7126, while 99.30 per cent of injected-template cases continued to satisfy the adopted detection criterion. Individual membership was less stable, with peripheral and locally sparse members showing lower persistence than structural cores. The deliberately overlapping pair was resolved spatially in only 15 of 1000 realisations; a reddening-based post-processing diagnostic increased this to 446, although with a corresponding completeness-purity trade-off. XMST therefore provides a robust method for identifying candidate stellar structures and their stable cores, while detailed outer membership and strongly overlapping populations require additional astrophysical information.
items.title: XMST: An Extended Minimum Spanning Tree Framework with Objective Fracture-Scale Selection

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) process long contexts, including long documents and lengthy conversations, but face token-level memory usage that increases proportionally to input length. Although model optimization and lossy prompt compression are widely used, these methods still fail to solve the long-context recall problem beyond pretrained and size-constrained context windows. This paper proposes a long-context recall method that maintains near-constant GPU memory usage as context length increases, without additional training. The main idea is to reconstruct facts using parameter activations in the LLM's feed-forward layers, which store residual vectors representing facts from the source document. Utilizing residual vectors allows the LLM to deterministically reconstruct query relevant facts without referencing the original document, preserving high fidelity and reducing memory usage without fine-tuning weights. Experimental results show that the proposed method enables answering single-fact questions in two-million-token story contexts where previous methods fail.
items.title: Residual Vector-based Reconstruction as Long-Context Recall Regardless of Context Window Size

items.summary: Periodic multilayer mirrors for X-rays require a layer period held to about 0.02 nm, set by deposition rates held in the laboratory's own notebook. A large language model agent was given a target multilayer specification and read access to a laboratory archive. Deposition recipes were authored in the native recipe language of a magnetron sputtering system and submitted through a Model Context Protocol bridge of 17 tools in three tiers, with enforcement held in the control application. The target was a 30-bilayer Ru/C multilayer with a period of 6.85 nm, a pair chosen because each period is fitted as two layers. The agent could write only inside a working project of its own, so it could alter neither the calibration it read nor the measurements that scored it. Mirrors were scored against a human-authored reference by X-ray reflectivity, and the 3% acceptance threshold on relative period difference was fixed before deposition. Across four scored agent-authored depositions the relative period difference fell from 20% on the calibration as given to 2.26% after one measured-feedback iteration and 0.79% after a second. Sixteen failure modes of the agent-facing interface were identified. The result is bounded to the period, pair and chamber observed.
items.title: Agent-authored deposition recipes for X-ray multilayer mirrors: schema-bound LLM control of a magnetron sputtering system with reflectivity-verified outcomes

items.summary: Agent evaluations can be numerically correct while measuring a different construct from the one implied by their labels. We present a retrospective measurement audit of selected Praxa AI implementation files, historical evaluation artifacts, and operational records. A 139-case offline routing report contains 112 passes and 27 failures despite zero gating failures, because known gaps are explicitly exempted from the gate. An identifier-free export represents 8,843 tool-attempt rows: 8,395 recorded durations and 448 missing values. Of the durations, 121 equal the signed 32-bit maximum and carry abandoned-client labels; inspected database code clamps elapsed lifecycle age. The pooled recorded 99th percentile is 2,147,483,647 ms, versus 38,118.31 ms among server-observed completed calls. This is a stratum contrast, not a treatment effect. In a documented single-trajectory compaction pilot, the reported follow-up input reduction is 94.39%, but the reduction across the trigger and follow-up calls together is 46.54%. We reproduce the descriptive calculations, verify 91 timing statistics through a separate weighted rational-arithmetic implementation, and execute 13 scoring-function and 12 analysis-verifier tests. Finite-completion bounds show how missing durations limit all-row timing statements without imputing values. The contribution is a source-linked case study and reusable verification package for separating gate policy, lifecycle timing, and request-level accounting from broader agent-performance claims. Historical provider runs and the full current pipeline were not independently reproduced; general capability superiority and population-level statistical significance are not established.
items.title: When Agent Metrics Measure Different Things: An Evidence-Grounded Audit of the Praxa AI Pipeline

items.summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.5321. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial tame knot type is at least 6.5321. This improves the 6.32 bound in version 1.0 by 0.2121. The proof combines essential-secant profiles, radial variational inequalities, ordered failure boundaries, and retained distortion constraints. The new comparison couples an actual last radial crossing on the initial arc with the same actual complementary split point, retaining both cyclic routes and common angular data. Necessary closed systems are excluded using directed interval arithmetic. Complete runs at 96-bit and 192-bit precision each certified all 54 original closed regions, testing 1,814,262 outer boxes per precision with no unresolved frontier. Independent mathematical, numerical and process-origin reviews passed. Fresh-extraction checks of the finished archive reproduced all 37 finite checks, the two-precision conditional component, and both full-receipt auditors. These checks supplement the complete original numerical runs. Version 2.0 contains the 19-page preprint and the complete reproducible LaTeX source and verification package, including frozen sources, full receipts, mathematical supplements, audit records and reproduction instructions. The package also documents structural research findings, unsuccessful approaches and remaining obstacles. No stronger global bound, knot upper bound, optimality, or proof-assistant formalization is claimed. The preprint has not been submitted to or accepted by a journal.
items.title: An improved lower bound for the distortion of a knotted curve

items.summary: Assistance can make a person's decision possible while leaving the person vulnerable to interpretive substitution and control of the available options. This paper develops a framework for adult disability support when will and preferences admit several warranted interpretations. Decision authorship is distinguished from causal responsiveness, functional performance, legal capacity, the validity of a particular act, and responsibility. A set-valued model separates semantic fidelity from authority over support and menus. Conditional results characterize compatible outcomes under interpretive uncertainty, changes under additional evidence, and the limited relation between menu expansion and compatibility. Counterexamples show that reversing every expressed preference satisfies sensitivity, that a constant outcome can satisfy fidelity, and that accurate selection within a restricted menu can coexist with an objectionable exclusion of alternatives. A temporal extension distinguishes learning about an earlier preference from forming a present preference through support. A finite branchwise result identifies when clarification permits compatible implementation despite an empty initial intersection. The normative discussion confronts CRPD Article 12, the Committee's corrected General Comment No. 1, selected provisions of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, and a prior proposal for interpretive support. A fictional community-participation decision demonstrates the audit, including disagreement, refusal, revision and supporter conflict. The resulting framework makes uncertainty and authority answerable without converting mathematical compatibility into permission to decide for another person. Empirical validation and case-specific legal application remain open.
items.title: Preserving Decision Authorship under Uncertain Interpretation of Will and Preferences in Adult Disability Support

items.summary: Structured quantum circuits are often represented by low-dimensional records such as occupation numbers or constraint feasibility rather than by full outcome distributions. A record loses control-dependent information when it merges outcomes whose probabilities respond differently to circuit parameters. We assess this loss without assuming a parametric hardware-noise model. Quantum Fisher information bounds premeasurement sensitivity; Fisher metrics of measurements and recorded statistics describe device-attainable sensitivity. For finite control changes, a Hellinger residual measures the response removed by a record, while its local quadratic term is the conditional covariance of the full-outcome score. Simultaneous confidence bounds support approval, refusal, or deferral. We prove a finite-library completion theorem: executable augmentations terminate either with a record preserving every declared response or with proof that no library augmentation removes the loss. For an analytic control germ, integral closures characterize preservation along every analytic control arc, and finitely many Rees valuations detect failure. This connects the state--measurement--record chain to an executable completion-or-refusal procedure, an attainable-Fisher kernel criterion, and finite-sample decisions. A three-qubit calculation separates measurement loss from record loss. Prospectively fixed IBM Kingston and Marrakesh experiments test decisions in four-qubit fixed-particle-number and GHZ families, including negative controls. In two-epoch IQM Garnet data, median record-level drift is 0.0797 times full-distribution drift, but a significant residual remains in 35 of 36 settings. On these circuits, the rules detect loss and approve records only within stated tolerances; they do not establish universal compression performance or device quantum Fisher information.
items.title: Completing or Refusing Low-Dimensional Records of Structured Quantum Circuits: Measurement Loss, Compression Loss, and Hardware Drift

items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
items.title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

items.summary: Languishing has predominantly been conceptualised at the level of the person, yet psychological constraint may also be expressed within particular configurations of thought. This qualitatively led mixed-methods study examined how university students’ person-level flourishing and NARMA languishing profiles related to self-identified cognitions that constrained movement towards personally meaningful flourishing futures. Seventy-five consenting participants at a South African university completed a 10-item NARMA Continuum comprising five PERMA-aligned flourishing indicators and five directly assessed NARMA languishing indicators: Negativity, Apathy, Restricted Relationships, Meaninglessness, and Adversity Preoccupation. Participants subsequently described a future flourishing self and completed a structured Target, Understand, Replace, and Nurture reflection. One consenting response contained insufficient substantive qualitative material, yielding 74 cases for qualitative analysis. Reflexive thematic analysis was combined with structured framework coding of three proposed properties of languishing cognition: Yield, the represented change in viable human possibility associated with a thought; Viability, the extent to which remaining possibility could still support meaningful participation; and Trajectory, the orientation of possibility towards narrowing, stalling, redirection, or widening. Quantitative scores were integrated as person-level case attributes. Target cognitions principally concerned anticipated failure or non-attainment (29.7%), stalled effort or mobilisation (20.3%), adversity or uncertainty (20.3%), and inadequacy or insufficient capability (13.5%). Yield was predominantly depletive (95.9%), yet depletion did not determine subsequent Trajectory. Viability was most commonly compromised but retained (56.8%), rather than extinguished, while Trajectory was mixed or redirecting in 48.6% of cases, narrowing in 21.6%, stalled in 16.2%, and widening in 13.5%. Overall flourishing and NARMA languishing were strongly inversely associated, r = -.762, 95% CI [-.843, -.647], p < .001. Exploratory integration showed that person-level flourishing differed across cognition-level Trajectory groups, H(3) = 12.69, p = .005, ε² = .14, whereas overall NARMA languishing did not, H(3) = 5.61, p = .132. Replacement cognitions most often restored agency through incremental progress, behavioural pathways, realistic self-permission, or action despite adversity. The findings support a cross-level distinction between person-level languishing and cognition-level constraint. They further suggest that the psychological significance of a thought may depend not only on its valence or content, but on what viable possibility it changes, what remains usable, and where possibility is oriented next. Keywords: languishing, NARMA, flourishing, cognition, viable human possibility, future selves, Yield, Viability, Trajectory, TURN

items.summary: Pre-registered results for Phase 22.D. The range-non-overlap criterion was to be tested on a genuinely unseen hold-out: Linear B sub-corpora from Thebes, Mycenae and Tiryns, harvested from DAMOS only after the pre-registration was published. The harvest yielded 617 tablets and 766 word tokens under the same L2_strict filter used for Knossos and Pylos, but fragmented across 27 series, of which only 3 reached the pre-declared minimum of 40 types. The pre-declared power gate required 5. No word-length class reached the 20-type floor, so the stratified primary test never ran. Verdict: TEST-VOID. With 3 observations the 99% prediction interval lower bound is -43.1 percent, an impossible value for a rate, which is precisely what the power gate exists to catch. The suspension of the Linear A / Linear B morphological gap imposed by Phase 22.B therefore becomes indefinite: the gap is real and is not a word-length artefact, but whether it demonstrates non-Mycenaean-Greekness remains untested. Descriptive figures are reported without verdict force. The only remaining route is the full DAMOS Knossos corpus rather than the def_strict subset. TERMINOLOGY: this project does not claim that Linear A "is not Greek"; the tested and rejected hypothesis is Mycenaean Greek. Pre-registration: doi 10.5281/zenodo.22749112. Version v2 (2026-09-15): OpenTimestamps proofs upgraded to confirmed Bitcoin block attestations. The pre-registration is anchored in blocks 966966, 966969 and 966971; the hold-out corpus and runner in blocks 967020, 967026 and 967042 — 54 blocks (approximately nine hours) later. The blindness of the test is therefore established by the Bitcoin blockchain rather than by declaration. No change to the data, the analysis, or the TEST-VOID verdict.
items.title: Phase 22.D Results: The Range Criterion Is Untestable on Available Unseen Mycenaean Data — A Pre-registered TEST-VOID Outcome.

items.summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.
items.title: Deriving the Pure Price of Anarchy for Networked Resource Allocation Games

items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. This version adds a new chapter on Cain, the altar, and the city of refuge — linking "from My altar you shall take him" (Exodus 21:14) to the Mishnah's ruling that one sentenced without a High Priest never goes free (Makkot 2:7), and to the discovery that Shechem itself is designated a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7. Additional sections trace Jacob's route from Sukkot to Shechem as a draft of Joshua's entry axis, the letter-midrash of "sotho" (Genesis 49:11) as a covering that was never performed, and the mechanical letter-echo of Shaddai hidden in Laban's Aramaic "Yegar Sahadutha" (Genesis 31:47).12:56 PM   The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place, 100,000 permutations yield T1 = 11.23 and T2 = 24.12, with zero exceedances (p_MC ≈ 10⁻⁵; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A Leave-One-Book-Out test shows no single Torah book is necessary for the signal (worst case: Genesis removed → Z = 10.61). A Leave-One-Motif-Out test shows no single root is necessary (worst: rbtz removed → Z = 16.01). A book-stratified null (Z = 19.93) confirms the effect is not an artifact of verse distribution. A top-10 ablation (Z = 3.95, p = 0.0013) shows the signal weakens but survives removal of the dominant motifs. A Foundation 12-Letter Split, stripping all 10 control letters rather than 7, yields Z = 4.17 — confirming the framework is not ad-hoc. Six benchmark anthologies were tested: the Ebal/Shechem axis is anomalous in all three validated methods; Covenant remains a positive control but significantly lower; Joseph, Tabernacle, and "the place that He will choose" are negative in all. An independent replication pilot tested whether the signal depends on the author's specific verse choices. Eight semantic criteria were defined — no roots, no letter analysis, no knowledge of any test results — and two independent language models selected Torah verses blind. Model A (243 verses) yielded T2 = 8.70; Model B (252 verses) yielded T2 = 9.84; the consensus of both (142 verses) yielded T2 = 8.51. All with zero exceedances. Only 22% of the essay's verses were also selected. The signal survives independent selection. A pre-registered protocol for three independent human readers is included (protocol hash: a577cb03...). The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual under multiple independent approaches. A dual adversarial computational audit (LLM-assisted) verified the code, reproduced the numbers, identified and corrected all bugs, and rated the statistical appendix at 7.0
items.title: The Earth That Listened — The Hidden Timeline from Genesis to Joshua

items.summary: AI coding assistants are becoming co-authors of production software, yet their evaluation centers on functional correctness, leaving open whether their code differs from human code in the quality dimensions dominating lifecycle cost. We compare human-written and AI-generated code at scale: 787,562 function pairs across Python, Java, and C, each human function mined from open-source repositories paired with implementations generated from its docstring by three AI assistants (OpenAI GPT models, DeepSeek-Coder, Qwen2.5-Coder). We characterize structural complexity and statistical naturalness, and map static-analysis findings onto Orthogonal Defect Classification for defects and the Common Weakness Enumeration for vulnerabilities, making authors and languages directly comparable. AI-generated code is structurally compressed and stylistically templated: roughly half the size and branching of human code, clustering apart at the style level. Defect profiles differ in kind: human code concentrates issues of mature codebases, AI code repetitive boilerplate; security is language-dependent, with LLMs producing more, and more severe, findings in Python and Java but fewer high-severity memory-safety findings than humans in C. Once size is controlled for, complexity metrics carry little signal, while naturalness separates authors. Finally, we release CQBench, a benchmark of 27,346 issue-prone tasks with baselines and an evaluation pipeline for quality assurance and security testing.
items.title: What is the Difference Between Me and You? Benchmarking the Quality Gap Between Human-Written and AI-Generated Code

items.summary: This archive contains public-safe derived data, analysis code, and verification records supporting the manuscript "Baseline bias shapes apparent skill changes under rainfall-input scaling in an urban flood surrogate." The package supports integrity checks and selected derived-analysis reruns for: the fixed-reference baseline–response boundary check; storage- and detection-threshold sensitivities; the separate 60-min auxiliary analysis; lead-time × rainfall-factor × tier sensitivity; internal-pathway aggregate diagnostics; rank-preserving area- and depth-index-matched spatial controls; and seed-level CSI direction counts (Supplementary Table S7g). Every file is covered by a SHA-256 inventory, and a self-contained verifier (verify_public_package.py) recomputes the recorded checks. The archive does not contain raw hydraulic inputs, the hydraulic solver or run controls, the source regional-frequency workbook, model checkpoints, restricted high-resolution response banks, or licensed basemap and satellite imagery. It therefore cannot reproduce model training, full inference, hydraulic simulations, or the map-based figures. The restricted source workbook and held-out forcing archive are represented by SHA-256 records and public-safe aggregate tables. Derived data and documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0; Python code is licensed under MIT (see LICENSE). This work was supported by an Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute (ETRI) grant funded by the Korean government [26ZR1300, Development of Technology for the Urban Extreme Rainfall Response Platform].

items.summary: Overview  This repository contains the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, surrogate model training scripts, NSGA-II multi-objective optimization suite, and raw experimental outputs supporting the manuscript: "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity" Abstract Traditional concrete mix design usually involves lengthy empirical trial-and-error procedures. This study proposes a CatBoost–NSGA-II framework for multi-objective optimisation of concrete mixes, including leakage-controlled evaluation, uncertainty-aware strength feasibility, repeated-run robustness, and strength-floor sensitivity analysis. To evaluate the surrogate models, a source-study-grouped evaluation protocol consisting of ten repeated train–test splits was employed. The compressive strength model obtained only moderate performance (R^2 = 0.654 ± 0.062), whereas the RCPT model exhibited unstable performance (R^2 = -1.01 ± 3.07) and was therefore not included in the optimisation constraints. An uncertainty-aware lower confidence bound was used for strength feasibility, and the buildability constraints were incorporated into NSGA-II. For the 40 MPa case, 20 separate runs resulted in a robust 15-member Pareto front with an 86.7% recurrence rate. The mixture chosen had estimated reductions of 50.0% in embodied carbon and 22.7% in material cost as compared with a baseline that had the same strength. Nevertheless, the benefits decreased as the strength floor was raised and became statistically no different from zero at 70 MPa. Experimental verification based on physical tests is necessary before the approach can be applied in practice. Repository Structure  * 1_data/: Processed concrete mix dataset (processed_dataset_1867_records.csv) and RCPT sub-dataset (rcpt_subset_203.csv).  * 2_code/: Python codebase including data_cleaner.py, train_catboost.py, nsga2_optimization.py, and run_full_pipeline.py.  * models/: Serialized .joblib CatBoost surrogate model binaries and uncertainty parameters.  * results/: Raw Pareto front outputs across 20 independent seed runs (pareto_front_seed_42.csv through seed_61.csv) and consolidated multi-run front metrics.  * Root: reproducibility_manifest.yaml, data_dictionary.csv, exclusion_log.csv, and main entrypoint run_all.py. Instructions for Reproducibility  * Extract concrete_mix_zenoda.zip.  * Install requirements: pip install -r 2_code/requirements.txt.  * Execute python run_all.py to re-run data cleaning, surrogate training, and multi-objective optimization.

items.summary: Code for the Paper "More Efficient Secret-Shared Joins with Multiplicity via Oblivious Sort Expansion" This repository contains the official implementation of the paper "More Efficient Secret-Shared Joins with Multiplicity via Oblivious Sort Expansion." The codebase includes our proposed protocols built on the SPU framework, as well as the source code for baseline comparisons. Project Structure 1. Our Implementation (Based on SPU) Located in Join-OSE/spu/sml/database/emulations/ . OSE : Implementation of the Oblivious Sort Expansion (OSE) along with correctness verification. Join-OM : Implements the Join-OM protocol from AHK+ ( Secure Statistical Analysis on Multiple Datasets: Join and Group-By ) and our Join-OM protocol based on OSE. Includes checks to verify identical outputs. Join-MM : Our main Join-MM protocol with working examples. Join-MM-32 : Parameterized version (32-bit inputs, adjustable input size) for benchmarks against BDG+ ( Secret-Shared Joins with Multiplicity from Aggregation Trees ). Includes correctness verification. Join-MM-64 : Parameterized version (64-bit inputs, adjustable input size) for benchmarks against Scape ( Scape: Scalable Collaborative Analytics System on Private Database with Malicious Security ). Join-MM-AggTree-32 : Implementation of the BDG+ Join-MM protocol, using 32-bit inputs. 2. Scape Baseline Located in Join-OSE/scql/engine/operator/secret_join.cc . Note on Modification : We have modified the secret_join.cc and secret_join_test.cc files to support runtime profiling and performance testing of Scape. items.summary: Assistance can make a person's decision possible while leaving the person vulnerable to interpretive substitution and control of the available options. This paper develops a framework for adult disability support when will and preferences admit several warranted interpretations. Decision authorship is distinguished from causal responsiveness, functional performance, legal capacity, the validity of a particular act, and responsibility. A set-valued model separates semantic fidelity from authority over support and menus. Conditional results characterize compatible outcomes under interpretive uncertainty, changes under additional evidence, and the limited relation between menu expansion and compatibility. Counterexamples show that reversing every expressed preference satisfies sensitivity, that a constant outcome can satisfy fidelity, and that accurate selection within a restricted menu can coexist with an objectionable exclusion of alternatives. A temporal extension distinguishes learning about an earlier preference from forming a present preference through support. A finite branchwise result identifies when clarification permits compatible implementation despite an empty initial intersection. The normative discussion confronts CRPD Article 12, the Committee's corrected General Comment No. 1, selected provisions of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, and a prior proposal for interpretive support. A fictional community-participation decision demonstrates the audit, including disagreement, refusal, revision and supporter conflict. The resulting framework makes uncertainty and authority answerable without converting mathematical compatibility into permission to decide for another person. Empirical validation and case-specific legal application remain open.
items.title: Preserving Decision Authorship under Uncertain Interpretation of Will and Preferences in Adult Disability Support

items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
items.title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

items.summary: An interface standard is advisory when nothing checks conformance to it, and normative when an external mechanism does. Python's public-interface convention is advisory: PEP 8 recommends that a library declare which symbols are contractual, but nothing enforces it, unlike Java, C++, or Rust. Every library therefore ships two surfaces at once — the declared surface it intends to support and the reachable surface clients can and do import — yet no prior work has measured how much of a library's surface is declared, how much of what clients consume is undeclared, or whether declaration predicts stability. We formalise a five-tier declaration ladder, computable statically from a distribution artifact, and measure it across 163 widely used libraries (81 AI/ML, 82 general-purpose controls) over up to 12 minor releases, together with a uniform sample of 30,000 PyPI projects yielding 14,213 client wheels and 12,704 clients contributing 419,752 import edges. The declared surface is tiny (only 7.4% of reachable symbols); clients over-select it by 5.9×, yet 56.5% (45.3% after a recall correction) of consumed edges remain undeclared, affecting 80.2% of client packages, though clients respect the underscore convention far more than __all__. Declaration status does predict removal — undeclared symbols disappear 1.5–2.5× as often as declared ones — and the AI/ML stack is not worse at signalling than general-purpose Python, only larger and faster-moving. The result is a repeatable, low-cost measurement that a standardisation process could run every release to check whether its own advisory recommendations are being followed.

items.summary: This document corresponds to the first release of the CLIM4cities MLOps Description and Validation (MLOps), deliverable D4 of the Work Package (WP) 4000, which pertains to the results obtained from reporting of the final Near-Surface Air Temperature [T2m] and Land Surface Temperature [LST] Machine Learning (ML) / Artificial Intelligence (AI) downscaling models. In this document, the description of the selected ML/AI model architectures is presented, along with performance metrics derived from unbiased data, i.e., reference datasets not used during training or fine-tuning. Special emphasis is given to error metrics on the tails of the statistical distribution of the target variables (T2m and LST) considering the desired outcome of having models that perform adequately in predicting temperatures during extreme events, such as heatwaves. Furthermore, the recognition of the underlying urban pattern is discussed, considering the requirements highlighted by the involved stakeholders since the early discussions of the CLIM4cities project (as reported in the Requirements Baseline (RB) deliverable (D1, from WP1000)). In D4, we offer a detailed description of the accomplished tasks, as follows: WP4100 – ECV 1 [LST]: Algorithm Description and Validation. WP4200 – ECV 2 [T2m]: Algorithm Description and Validation. WP4300 – Proof of Concept Application: Climate Atlas and UHI. A fourth section, ‘WP4400 - Scientific Assessment of ML model for climate scenarios for Urban Climate Adaptation’ is also envisaged, following the Contract Change Notice (CCN). extension, taking advantage of the ongoing efforts in modelling additional cities (Seville, Athens, Lisbon and Copenhagen) using a European dataset (CERRA) and assimilating optical-based vegetation indices (NDVI) as a key predictor to account for the phenological cycle of the green infrastructure of the cities, allowing to disentangle the seasonal cycle of vegetation. These updates shall follow the CCN updates on deliverables D2 (ML Architectures Benchmark Report) and D3 (Non-EO and GEO Data Collection), and be delivered by May 2026. In this report, CLIM4cities outlines: the best-fitted LST model, which entails a description of employing a multi-timestamp approach, suitable for an operational setting where image-specific modelling is less desirable. Here, we discuss the advantages and limitations of adopting an ML architecture for Sentinel-3 LST Downscaling, versus a linear regression, by using Landsat as the biased reference, while recognising that there are inherited differences between the LST products of both missions. We also highlight the limits of the scale-invariance approach. the best-fitted T2m model, which focuses on validating the performance of the Random Forest approach in the space and time domain of station observations not used in training/fine-tuning, including against WMO stations. Furthermore, we discuss the advantages and limitations of the model concerning representativeness of urban-rural differences, recognising the unbalanced nature of the input dataset, particularly the overrepresentation of observations in urban areas. How well do these models reflect the urban-rural differences and respond to the expressed needs of the stakeholders, highlighting the key patterns of the Urban Heat Island (UHI), calculated as the urban-rural difference, over representative sampling areas. Furthermore, differences between T2m and LST are discussed, showcasing how each ECV offers different perspectives on the UHI effect and how this information can inform climate adaptation at the urban scale.

items.summary: This document corresponds to the final release of the CLIM4cities Non-EO Selection and Harmonization Report (NEOR), deliverable D3 of the Work Package (WP)3000, which explains the rationale for choosing the selected non-EO data sources, its harmonisation and processing approach, and its added value for the ML model performance in WP2000. Adding to the provisions made in the original Invitation to Tender (ITT) documentation, CLIM4cities has addressed WP3000 as an overall data collection and pre-processing step of the project, resulting in the final ML model database. Hence, this WP reports all the datasets gathered, their sources and characteristics, along with the full description of the pre-processing sets required for quality control, conversions into derived variables, collocation and harmonisation into the final dataset used for the Machine Learning (ML) training (reported in WP2000, D2 Benchmark Report). The NEOR reports on the following tasks within WP3000 Non-EO and GEO Data Collection, organised into sequential sections of this report: WP3100 - Crowdsourced Data Collection and Quality Assurance, which includes gathering the information from the Citizen Weather Stations (CWS) with available and dense data for the three main cities of study of Denmark - Copenhagen, and at least two out of Aarhus, Odense and Aalborg - with the characterization and application of quality control methodologies. WP3200 - Geospatial Data Collection and Processing, focusing on developing and describing the geospatial data suitable for the development of the CLIM4cities air temperature and land surface temperature (T2m and LST, respectively) models. WP3300 - ML Database Collocation and Harmonization, reporting the final data wrangling steps towards setting up (i) a single collocated regular grid of predictors and (ii) the time series (point-wise, at each CWS station location) to serve as the training input for the CLIM4cities T2m and LST model development.  WP3400 - Data Collection and Exploratory Data Analysis [T2m] in additional FUAs, reports the additional data collection associated with the added functional urban areas, Athens and Seville, as well as the NDVI data used in the updated CERRA based model. items.summary: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. Existing agentic memory systems address this limitation but generally operate at the individual-user level, restricting the public knowledge that could be shared across users to improve downstream responses. We introduce AIM (Agentic Interoperable Memory), a unified, privacy-aware memory framework that enables multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems to persistently manage private and shared memory. AIM dynamically classifies information as private, scoped to one user and inaccessible to others, or public, accessible to all users. It enforces index-level access controls so that private memories are retrievable only by their owner, protecting sensitive data while allowing beneficial shared knowledge to improve coordination and consistency. We also introduce MUMBench (Multi-User Memory Benchmark), a dataset of multi-user interactions containing private and shareable information across four domains. To our knowledge, MUMBench is the first public dataset designed to evaluate multiple memory operations, including retrieval, creation, update, and deletion, in a multi-user environment. Across three independent runs on MUMBench, AIM achieves 96.0% visibility classification accuracy, 58.8% strict operation accuracy, and 70.5% state-aware operation accuracy.
items.title: AIM: A Privacy-Aware Interoperable Memory Framework for Multi-Agent Multi-User LLM Systems

items.summary: Significant progress has been made in safeguarding deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies against input perturbations. Developing robust DRL involves three main stages: algorithm design, implementation, and evaluation. In this work, we identify and address a key limitation at each stage. First, we introduce Adversarial Importance Sampling (Advis), a method that uses importance sampling over trajectories from standard training to estimate and optimize verifiable worst-case returns. Advis satisfies three desirable criteria not jointly achieved by prior work: it requires no additional environment interactions, no auxiliary networks, and captures long-term robustness. Second, we introduce advrl, a modular PyTorch library that provides clean, single-file implementations of existing robustness methods and adversarial attacks, facilitating rapid prototyping and enabling reproducible and traceable evaluations. Third, we revisit evaluation under learned adversaries and show that optimal adversarial hyperparameters do not transfer across agents, which can lead to an overestimation of robustness when using a limited set of attacker configurations. Accordingly, we evaluate policies against a large and diverse set of attackers, using 6-14x more configurations than prior work. Finally, we evaluate our approach on continuous control environments, demonstrating its effectiveness relative to existing baselines. The code is available at: https://github.com/AmineAndam04/advrl
items.title: Robust Policy Optimization via Adversarial Importance Sampling

items.summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. Robustness checks include Newey–West HAC standard errors, alternative bandwidths, leave-one-out tests, influential-year exclusions, winsorization, placebo leads, and multiple-testing corrections using the Benjamini–Hochberg, Holm, and Bonferroni procedures. All data preparation and statistical analyses were conducted in R. The results show that Turkish and Greek naval procurement processes are temporally connected rather than independent. The strongest delivery-to-delivery association appears at a two-year lag. Greek naval deliveries are also associated with Turkish international naval orders one year later, while reverse-direction models identify associations between Turkish deliveries and subsequent Greek international orders. The overall pattern is consistent with reciprocal and temporally clustered modernization cycles rather than a fixed one-way action–reaction process. The repository includes cleaned analytical datasets, R scripts, figures, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, citation metadata, and the manuscript. Raw proprietary or redistribution-restricted source files are not included; users should consult the original SIPRI and World Bank sources where applicable. Version 1.2 adds the reviewer-requested stationarity diagnostics, first-difference sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-programme-window-out tests. The revised package also includes updated regression outputs and the reviewer-revised manuscript. The main research design and core delivery-to-delivery finding remain unchanged.
items.title: Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025: Replication Data and Code

items.summary: Accurate prediction of equity returns remains a major challenge in computational finance due to the non-stationary, nonlinear, and low signal-to-noise ratio nature of financial time series. This paper proposes a hybrid two-stage architecture that combines a long short-term memory (LSTM) network with an XGBoost gradient-boosted regressor for multi-horizon stock return prediction across a diversified panel of 14 U.S. equities spanning six industry sectors. The LSTM component, comprising two stacked layers with 64 hidden units, processes 60-day sliding windows of five sequential market features to produce 64-dimensional temporal embeddings that encode learned sequential market dynamics. These embeddings are concatenated with 14 hand-crafted technical indicators to form a 78-dimensional hybrid feature vector, which is subsequently passed to an XGBoost regressor tuned via 3-fold cross-validation grid search. The framework is trained on a multi-stock pooled corpus using strict chronological splits and per-stock MinMaxScaling to prevent look-ahead bias, and evaluated across four prediction horizons of 30, 90, 252, and 365 trading days. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid model achieves a test RMSE of 0.0949 on the 30-day horizon, roughly one-third that of the standalone LSTM baseline, while marginally matching or surpassing the XGBoost-Only baseline across the majority of stocks. Directional accuracy rises with horizon length, reaching 97.6% at 365 days; we show, however, that this largely tracks the high base rate of positive long-horizon returns in the sample, and we therefore benchmark directional accuracy against a naive always-positive predictor and treat the above-base-rate gap at short horizons as the more informative signal. A composite investment scoring framework derived from multi-horizon predictions is further proposed to support portfolio ranking and decision support.
items.title: A Hybrid LSTM-XGBoost Framework for Multi-Horizon Stock Return Prediction Across Diversified Equity Portfolios

items.summary: This record contains the reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript “A Projected Semiexplicit Integrator for Dissipative Systems with Configuration-Dependent Kinetic Energy: Contact-Herglotz Formulation and Benchmarks.” The package provides the Julia implementation, pinned computational environment, benchmark parameters, analysis and plotting scripts, automated tests, CSV result files, generated figures and LaTeX table bodies, and per-run metadata supporting the results reported in the manuscript and its Supplementary Material. The implementation covers the projected semiexplicit contact-Herglotz integrator and the numerical benchmarks used to assess convergence, contact and conformal structure preservation, projection activity and load, long-time behavior, work-precision performance, variable friction, Tao extended-phase-space baselines, Kevrekidis-type contact splittings, and the lifted implicit midpoint comparison. A single documented driver, analysis/run_all.jl , regenerates the numerical results, tables, and figures used by the study. The archived environment requires Julia 1.12 or later, and the reported results were generated with Julia 1.12.6. The source code is distributed under the MIT License. Generated results and documentation are distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0). Associated preprint: arXiv:2608.17198.
items.title: Reproducibility package for "A Projected Semiexplicit Integrator for Dissipative Systems with Configuration-Dependent Kinetic Energy: Contact-Herglotz Formulation and Benchmarks"

items.summary: Long-running LLM agents require memory mechanisms that maintain coherent internal states across interactions. We study a lifecycle-labeled memory setting in which write episodes provide lifecycle metadata during training, and phase-aware readout is used during evaluation. This setting reflects the need to distinguish information that should remain influential across future interactions from information that should affect only the current context. A mismatch between these lifecycles can cause temporary information to overwrite durable knowledge, leading to behavioral drift in persistent agents. Within this setting, we introduce \textbf{LifeFuse-Mem}, a lifecycle-aware neural memory framework that separates information according to its temporal commitment. LifeFuse-Mem uses dedicated memory components and lifecycle-aware updates to allow stable and transient knowledge to evolve locally without converting temporary context into durable state. On the controlled anti-overwrite benchmark, LifeFuse-Mem improves acquisition-controlled retention and reduces temporary overwrite; on two public long-memory benchmarks, it remains broadly competitive. These results suggest that explicit lifecycle signals can help diagnose and mitigate overwrite in compact online memory.
items.title: LifeFuse-Mem: Lifecycle-Aware State Fusion Against Temporary Overwriting for Long-Term Memory

items.summary: A configurable and reproducible benchmark for developing and evaluating autonomous systems in underwater gate-racing tasks, built on HoloOcean with a BlueROV2-class vehicle. Controllers operate exclusively from onboard observations, acoustic measurements and optional inter-vehicle communication, while an independent referee accesses privileged simulator state only to validate ordered gate crossings, enforce the rules and compute the official results.
items.title: Marine Race Arena

items.summary: Production artificial intelligence systems are increasingly assessed not only by whether they generate accurate predictions, but by whether the operating organization can reconstruct, explain, and defend the exact evidence behind an individual outcome after the surrounding system has changed. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring that property, which we term evidence continuity. The framework is grounded primarily and foundationally in the work of Mesbaul Haque Sazu, specifically his Governed Decision-Intelligence (GDI) reference architecture [22] and his Full-Stack Production-Platform Reference Architecture [21]. GDI establishes the decision as the unit of assurance and makes evidence binding, lineage, validation, calibrated confidence, deterministic explanation, human oversight, and outcome closure explicit control obligations. The Full-Stack architecture extends these obligations into runtime operation through capture-at-commit, execution records, trajectory-level observability, before-commit gating, and closed-loop production control. Building directly on and leveraging these two foundations, this paper contributes a measurement layer that sits above them. We model an AI system as a typed, versioned, directed evidence graph and introduce three constructs: the Evidence Continuity Graph (ECG), the Trace Completeness Ratio (TCR), and the Governance Coverage Index (GCI). We formalize per-decision and aggregate estimators, extend the naive independence model to a correlated-failure regime using a Beta-Binomial mixture, and derive path-based reconstructability over admissible evidence paths. A synthetic benchmark of 2,800 investigation traces demonstrates how time-to-trace, incomplete-trace probability, and reconstruction probability respond as evidence coverage varies. The results are illustrative rather than empirical claims about deployed systems. The paper concludes with a reference implementation architecture, threshold-setting guidance calibrated to deployment risk, a security and failure analysis, and a research agenda for validating evidence continuity on real production workloads.

items.summary: Flow matching approaches to imaging inverse problems commonly incorporate measurements in two ways. Conditioning-based approaches supply measurement-derived information as a network input, often through concatenation, while inference-guided approaches combine an unconditional velocity field with a separate data-consistency update. In these common formulations, the forward model is not explicitly enforced within the learned conditional velocity field. We propose a principled parametrization of the measurement-conditional velocity field to solve inverse problems. Under linear interpolation, we express the conditional velocity $v(x_t,t,y)$ in terms of the posterior mean $E[x_1 | x_t,y]$, and characterize that mean as the unique minimizer of a variational objective whose data-consistency term is explicit. We further prove that the velocity field defines a probability flow from the source distribution to the measurement-conditioned posterior. Splitting the variational objective yields a conditional velocity parameterization with operator-dependent data-consistency updates, which we train end-to-end under the flow-matching objective, with no additional guidance at inference. Our method achieves state-of-the-art PSNR with $50\times$ fewer function evaluations than the strongest flow baseline. Varying the sampling steps provides test-time control over the distortion-perception trade-off without retraining.
items.title: Fast and Faithful: Principled Conditional Flow Matching for Inverse Problems

items.summary: Traditional contemplative interventions often face significant geographical, logistical, and socio-economic barriers that limit their accessibility, scalability, and standardized implementation in public health settings. This study evaluates the methodological feasibility, instructional fidelity, and psychological efficacy of a 28-day virtually delivered Rajyoga meditation curriculum administered via synchronous online video conferencing (Zoom). Operating within a quasi-experimental design, 312 novice practitioners were assigned across three intervention arms: Pre-Dawn Synchronous Amritvela Meditation (G1, n = 110; 4:00 AM–4:45 AM), Evening Synchronous Meditation (G2, n = 100; 8:30 PM–9:15 PM), and a No-Meditation Control Group (G3, n = 102). Standardized assessments were completed pre- and post-intervention using the Spiritual Well-Being Scale (SWBS) and the Spirituality Index of Well-Being (SIWB). Digital tracking yielded a 100% completion rate (zero attrition) and exceptional daily attendance compliance across both virtual groups. Paired t-tests demonstrated massive post-intervention improvements in both virtual cohorts, with the Amritvela cohort exhibiting superior gains on SWBS (Gain = +8.81, t(109) = 10.49, p < .001, Cohen's d = 1.00) and SIWB (Gain = +9.74, t(109) = 13.47, p < .001, Cohen's d = 1.28) compared to the Evening cohort (SWBS Gain = +6.26, d = 0.75; SIWB Gain = +5.65, d = 0.88), while the Control group exhibited slight decline or stasis. Mixed-design ANOVA revealed highly significant Time × Group interaction effects for both SWBS (F(2,309) = 59.27, p < .001, partial eta^2 = .277) and SIWB (F(2,309) = 71.68, p < .001, partial eta^2 = .317). ANCOVA confirmed that virtual intervention gains held firmly after baseline adjustment. These findings establish synchronous virtual delivery as a high-fidelity, methodologically rigorous, and scalable framework for delivering structured contemplative interventions without compromising therapeutic potency or spiritual transformation.
items.title: Methodological Innovations in Spiritual Interventions: Virtual Delivery of Rajyoga Meditation

items.summary: Lux AI Season 3 requires agents to act under partial observability, randomized episode level dynamics, and a best of five match structure that rewards both tactical execution and fast adaptation. We present HORIZON, a hierarchical agent that combines symmetry aware spatial perception, dual memory belief tracking, relic centric graph attention, information gain driven exploration, and an opponent conditioned policy mixture. HORIZON separates short horizon control from cross match meta reasoning, while auxiliary belief and world model objectives stabilize learning. Trained with PPO in a large scale JAX simulator, the resulting agent explicitly infers hidden game parameters and opponent style. Experiments show consistent gains in match win rate, episode win rate, adaptation gain, and league rating over strong recurrent and feed forward baselines.
items.title: Hierarchical Belief Modeling for Zero-Shot Opponent Adaptation in Partially Observable Multi-Agent Navigation

items.summary: Agentic systems offer a promising way to automate embodied benchmark construction, but existing approaches typically cover isolated stages or remain specialized to predefined environments and task families. More importantly, multi-step construction produces dependent intermediate artifacts that are often passed downstream without artifact-specific verification, allowing local defects to propagate into the final benchmark. We present Embodied-BenchForge, an agentic framework that transforms user-specified evaluation intents into complete embodied benchmark artifacts. It formulates construction as Closed-Loop Benchmark Synthesis, integrating forward artifact synthesis with backward verification and repair. Skill-Orchestrated Artifact Synthesis composes typed and reusable skills into executable workflows, while an artifact dependency graph records intermediate outputs and their dependencies. Requirement-Guided Verification and Repair applies artifact-specific contracts throughout construction and uses provenance to trigger local re-execution or upstream rollback when verification fails. Embodied-BenchForge constructs six benchmarks covering diverse embodied scenarios in the Offline EQA Track, together with one interactive benchmark containing 220 executable tasks in the Interactive Embodied Track. Evaluations of representative MLLMs and embodied agents show that the benchmarks distinguish model capabilities in both observation-based understanding and closed-loop execution. Quality assessment and ablations validate benchmark quality and the effectiveness of verification and repair, while repair and skill-reuse analyses demonstrate efficient localized recovery and cross-benchmark reusability.
items.title: Embodied-BenchForge: A Closed-Loop Agentic Workflow for Embodied Benchmark Construction

items.summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Author identity is withheld pending the outcome of review. The package contains two independently generated archives: (1) model-I-single-branch/ — a single clock-controlled ternary LFSR generator over GF(3) (controller LFSR A + data LFSR B), together with its exact period and design-condition checkers, a statistical analysis suite, a 14-family ternary long-sequence test battery, and a cryptanalytic attack suite (basic correlation, embedding, fast correlation, Berlekamp-Massey reconstruction, and a linear-consistency/clock-control attack). Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
items.title: Reproducibility package for "Clock-Controlled Ternary Sequence Generators over GF(3): Exact Periods, Statistical Structure, and Cryptanalytic Comparison of Single-Branch and Three-Branch Nonlinear Architectures"
